name: Ballew 2015 CINDER model-to-model benchmark
description: Source-constrained reconstruction of Ballew's five-second simulated ATV/CVT acceleration case, re-run against cinder-cvt 1.0.0. This is not experimental validation.

source.citation: Brian Gene Ballew, Investigation Of A Numerical Algorithm For A Discretized Rubber-Belt Continuously Variable Transmission Dynamic Model And Techniques For The Measurement Of Belt Material Properties, M.S. thesis, University of Arkansas, 2015.

comparison_scope.force_replay: Impose digitized Ballew Figure 45 primary clamp force on unchanged CINDER and compare Figure 41 shaft speeds and derived speed ratio.
comparison_scope.closed_loop: Apply Ballew's published PI + feed-forward gains through the documented A11 controller reconstruction around unchanged CINDER; compare Figure 41 speeds/ratio and Figure 45 primary clamp demand.

reference_data.preparation_policy: No smoothing, filtering, resampling, curve fitting, or controller reconstruction. Preserve native Figure 41 grids; average exact duplicate Figure 45 times; prepend the first visible Figure 45 force to t=0 with zero-order hold.

contract_note: Ballew requires tabulated and PI-controlled primary axial-force laws. CINDER 1.0.0 intentionally leaves custom Python force laws and hosts as Python extension points rather than serializing them as built-ins. This study validates the assembled CVT through cinder.contracts.validate_assembly, runs only the installed cinder-cvt==1.0.0 package, and writes every published/reconstructed extension parameter to resolved_study.json.
